Data Analysis - Behaviours

Interaction Behaviours x Sex: A treatment × sex interaction was included to test whether the behavioural response to fluoxetine differed between males and females. This is biologically relevant because sex-specific differences in immune activation and sickness behaviour have been reported in vertebrates and may influence responses to environmental contaminants.

Behaviour: Distance_moved x Sex

The total distance (in cm) that fish swim during the behavioural trial. Tank_ID was firstly included in the analysis as a random factor, but the data indicated that, for all behavioural responses, tanks do not explain any addtional variation beyond the residual error. When the model was not singular, tank_ID was removed.

# Prepare variables
data$treatment <- factor(data$treatment,
                       levels = c("control", "low", "high"))

data$sex <- factor(data$sex)
data$tank_id <- factor(data$tank_id)
data$body_mass_sc <- scale(data$body_mass)


# Interaction (full) model
m_distance_int <- lm(
  distance_cm ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc,
  data = data
)

summary(m_distance_int)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = distance_cm ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc, data = data)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -1409.6  -766.9  -159.9   530.9  3405.7 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                       Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)            1072.80     190.73   5.625 9.01e-08 ***
## treatmentlow            280.99     264.74   1.061    0.290    
## treatmenthigh           -16.04     270.12  -0.059    0.953    
## sexmale                -129.33     266.76  -0.485    0.629    
## body_mass_sc            -24.60      79.51  -0.309    0.757    
## treatmentlow:sexmale    204.06     370.92   0.550    0.583    
## treatmenthigh:sexmale   437.61     373.44   1.172    0.243    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 945.1 on 148 degrees of freedom
##   (1 observation deleted due to missingness)
## Multiple R-squared:  0.03915,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.0001946 
## F-statistic: 1.005 on 6 and 148 DF,  p-value: 0.4244
# Diagnosis
res_m1_distance_moved_int <- simulateResiduals(m_distance_int)
plot(res_m1_distance_moved_int)

testDispersion(res_m1_distance_moved_int)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.96355, p-value = 0.688
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testZeroInflation(res_m1_distance_moved_int)

## 
##  DHARMa zero-inflation test via comparison to expected zeros with
##  simulation under H0 = fitted model
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## ratioObsSim = NaN, p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_m1_distance_moved_int)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_m1_distance_moved_int
## outliers at both margin(s) = 0, observations = 155, p-value = 0.6397
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.00000000 0.02351825
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                                      0
#Anova of the model
Anova(m_distance_int, type = "III")
## Anova Table (Type III tests)
## 
## Response: distance_cm
##                  Sum Sq  Df F value    Pr(>F)    
## (Intercept)    28258107   1 31.6369 9.008e-08 ***
## treatment       1420343   2  0.7951    0.4535    
## sex              209935   1  0.2350    0.6285    
## body_mass_sc      85509   1  0.0957    0.7574    
## treatment:sex   1227661   2  0.6872    0.5046    
## Residuals     132193525 148                      
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
emmeans(m_distance_int, pairwise ~ treatment | sex, adjust = "tukey")
## $emmeans
## sex = female:
##  treatment emmean  SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
##  control     1073 191 148      696     1450
##  low         1354 187 148      985     1723
##  high        1057 194 148      673     1440
## 
## sex = male:
##  treatment emmean  SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
##  control      944 183 148      581     1306
##  low         1429 188 148     1056     1801
##  high        1365 182 148     1005     1725
## 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## 
## $contrasts
## sex = female:
##  contrast       estimate  SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  control - low    -281.0 265 148  -1.061  0.5395
##  control - high     16.0 270 148   0.059  0.9981
##  low - high        297.0 268 148   1.110  0.5093
## 
## sex = male:
##  contrast       estimate  SE  df t.ratio p.value

##  control - high   -421.6 258 148  -1.637  0.2336
##  low - high         63.5 261 148   0.243  0.9679
## 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates
emmeans(m_distance_int, pairwise ~ sex | treatment, adjust = "tukey")

Plotting Distance_moved x Sex

# Prepare labels
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control", "low", "high")),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    ),
    sex_plot = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("female", "male"),
      labels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  )

# Estimated marginal means for treatment × sex interaction
emm_distance_int_df <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(
    m_distance_int,
    ~ sex | treatment
  )
)

cn <- names(emm_distance_int_df)

mean_col  <- dplyr::first(cn[cn %in% c("response", "rate", "emmean")])

lower_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^lower\\.CL$|^asymp\\.LCL$|^LCL$|^lower$", cn)]
)

upper_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^upper\\.CL$|^asymp\\.UCL$|^UCL$|^upper$", cn)]
)

emm_distance_int_df <- emm_distance_int_df %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control", "low", "high")),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    ),
    sex_plot = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("female", "male"),
      labels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(
    mean  = !!mean_col,
    lower = !!lower_col,
    upper = !!upper_col
  )

# Colour palettes for sex

sex_pastel_cols <- c(
  "Female" = "#D8B4E2",
  "Male"   = "#A9CCE3"
)

sex_dark_cols <- c(
  "Female" = "#8E44AD",
  "Male"   = "#2874A6"
)


# Plot: sex side by side within treatment
pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.75)

pj <- position_jitterdodge(
  jitter.width = 0.12,
  dodge.width = 0.75
)

p_distance_int_side <- ggplot() +

  geom_violin(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = distance_cm,
      fill = sex_plot,
      group = interaction(treatment_plot, sex_plot)
    ),
    position = pd,
    trim = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.25,
    colour = NA,
    linewidth = 0
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = distance_cm,
      colour = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pj,
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_distance_int_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      colour = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pd,
    width = 0.18,
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = emm_distance_int_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = mean,
      fill = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pd,
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_dark_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_pastel_cols) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 4000),
    breaks = seq(0, 4000, by = 500),
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Distance moved (cm)",
    fill = "Sex",
    colour = "Sex"
  ) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13)
  )

print(p_distance_int_side)

Main effects model

# Linear model
m_distance <- lm(
  distance_cm ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc,
  data = data
)

summary(m_distance)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = distance_cm ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc, data = data)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -1411.7  -751.5  -154.0   567.3  3515.0 
##

Plotting

Behaviour: Distance_moved

#---------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Ensure treatment order
#---------------------------------------------------------

data$treatment <- factor(
  data$treatment,
  levels = c("control", "low", "high")
)

# Labels for plotting
data$treatment_plot <- factor(
  data$treatment,
  levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
  labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
)

#---------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Fit final model
#---------------------------------------------------------

m_distance <- lm(
  distance_cm ~ treatment + sex + body_mass,
  data = data
)

summary(m_distance)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = distance_cm ~ treatment + sex + body_mass, data = data)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -1411.7  -751.5  -154.0   567.3  3515.0 
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)    1056.03     277.56   3.805 0.000206 ***
## treatmentlow    387.47     185.08   2.093 0.037989 *  
## treatmenthigh   213.16     185.94   1.146 0.253468    
## sexmale          85.69     158.13   0.542 0.588717    
## body_mass      -142.24     382.92  -0.371 0.710811    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 943.1 on 150 degrees of freedom
##   (1 observation deleted due to missingness)
## Multiple R-squared:  0.03022,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.004364 
## F-statistic: 1.169 on 4 and 150 DF,  p-value: 0.3269
Anova(m_distance, type = "II")
## Anova Table (Type II tests)
## 
## Response: distance_cm
##              Sum Sq  Df F value Pr(>F)
## treatment   3912025   2  2.1991 0.1145
## sex          261163   1  0.2936 0.5887
## body_mass    122739   1  0.1380 0.7108
## Residuals 133421186 150
#---------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Estimated marginal means
#---------------------------------------------------------

emm_dist_df <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(m_distance, ~ treatment)
)

print(emm_dist_df)
##  treatment   emmean       SE  df  lower.CL upper.CL
##  control   1004.041 130.8237 150  745.5459 1262.536
##  low       1391.507 130.8825 150 1132.8951 1650.118
##  high      1217.203 132.2857 150  955.8186 1478.587
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: sex 
## Confidence level used: 0.95
#---------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Standardise column names
#---------------------------------------------------------

cn <- names(emm_dist_df)

mean_col  <- dplyr::first(cn[cn %in% c("response", "rate", "emmean")])

lower_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^lower\\.CL$|^asymp\\.LCL$|^LCL$|^lower$", cn)]
)

upper_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^upper\\.CL$|^asymp\\.UCL$|^UCL$|^upper$", cn)]
)

if (is.na(mean_col) | is.na(lower_col) | is.na(upper_col)) {
  stop("Could not identify CI columns.")
}

emm_dist_df <- emm_dist_df %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high")
    ),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(
    mean  = !!mean_col,
    lower = !!lower_col,
    upper = !!upper_col
  )

#---------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Colour palette
#---------------------------------------------------------

pastel_cols <- c(
  "Control" = "#A8D5BA",
  "Low"     = "#F9E79F",
  "High"    = "#F5B7B1"
)

dark_cols <- c(
  "Control" = "#2E8B57",
  "Low"     = "#C9A227",
  "High"    = "#B22222"
)

#---------------------------------------------------------
# 6) Plot
#---------------------------------------------------------

p_distance <- ggplot() +

  geom_violin(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = distance_cm,
      fill = treatment_plot
    ),
    trim = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.35,
    colour = NA
  ) +

  geom_jitter(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = distance_cm,
      colour = treatment_plot
    ),
    width = 0.18,
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_dist_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      colour = treatment_plot
    ),
    width = 0.25,
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = emm_dist_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = mean,
      fill = treatment_plot
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = dark_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pastel_cols) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 3000),
    breaks = seq(0, 3000, by = 500),
    labels = comma
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Distance moved (cm)"
  ) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13)
  )

print(p_distance)

Refuge duration x sex

Refuge_duration: time that fish spend under the shelter during the trials.Refuge duration exhibited a zero-inflated continuous distribution, with approximately 13% of fish never entering the refuge (0 s). To appropriately model this response, a Tweedie GLM was fitted because the Tweedie distribution accommodates continuous positive values while allowing an exact mass at zero, making it well suited for ecological time-to-event and duration data with excess zeros.

# Model: family Tweedie
m_refuge_int <- glmmTMB(
  refuge_duration_s ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc +
    (1 | tank_id),
  family = tweedie(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m_refuge_int)
##  Family: tweedie  ( log )
## Formula:          
## refuge_duration_s ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   2016.6   2047.0   -998.3   1996.6      145 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance  Std.Dev. 
##  tank_id (Intercept) 4.213e-09 6.491e-05
## Number of obs: 155, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion parameter for tweedie family (): 13.9 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                       Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)            5.69972    0.21249  26.823   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow          -0.07596    0.29522  -0.257   0.7970    
## treatmenthigh          0.19502    0.29242   0.667   0.5048    
## sexmale                0.49696    0.28542   1.741   0.0817 .  
## body_mass_sc          -0.08629    0.08601  -1.003   0.3157    
## treatmentlow:sexmale  -0.07783    0.39695  -0.196   0.8445    
## treatmenthigh:sexmale -0.73002    0.40142  -1.819   0.0690 .  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# Diagnosis

simulationOutput <- simulateResiduals(m_refuge_int)
plot(simulationOutput)

testDispersion(simulationOutput)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.77975, p-value = 0.208
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testZeroInflation(simulationOutput)

## 
##  DHARMa zero-inflation test via comparison to expected zeros with
##  simulation under H0 = fitted model
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## ratioObsSim = 1.1421, p-value = 0.6
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(simulationOutput)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## outliers at both margin(s) = 0, observations = 155, p-value = 0.6397
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.00000000 0.02351825
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                                      0
#Anova of the model
Anova(m_refuge_int, type = "III")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: refuge_duration_s
##                  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
## (Intercept)   719.4962  1    < 2e-16 ***
## treatment       0.9203  2    0.63119    
## sex             3.0316  1    0.08166 .  
## body_mass_sc    1.0065  1    0.31574    
## treatment:sex   3.9046  2    0.14194    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
emm_refuge_int <- emmeans(
    m_refuge_int,
    ~ treatment | sex,
    type = "response"
)

pairs(
    emm_refuge_int,
    adjust = "tukey"
)
## sex = female:
##  contrast       ratio    SE  df null z.ratio p.value
##  control / low  1.079 0.319 Inf    1   0.257  0.9642
##  control / high 0.823 0.241 Inf    1  -0.667  0.7827
##  low / high     0.763 0.223 Inf    1  -0.928  0.6226
## 
## sex = male:
##  contrast       ratio    SE  df null z.ratio p.value
##  control / low  1.166 0.310 Inf    1   0.579  0.8312
##  control / high 1.707 0.469 Inf    1   1.948  0.1254
##  low / high     1.464 0.414 Inf    1   1.347  0.3691
## 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Tests are performed on the log scale
emmeans(
    m_refuge_int,
    pairwise ~ sex | treatment,
    type = "response",
    adjust = "tukey"
)

Velocity * sex

Average swimming speed of each fish during the behavioural trial, calculated from the distance travelled over time and expressed in centimetres per second (cm/s)

# Linear model
m_velo_int <- lm(
  velocity_cm.s ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc,
  data = data
)

summary(m_velo_int)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = velocity_cm.s ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc, 
##     data = data)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -1.1691 -0.6259 -0.1103  0.5387  2.7701 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                       Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)            0.96330    0.15855   6.076 9.97e-09 ***
## treatmentlow           0.16825    0.22221   0.757   0.4502    
## treatmenthigh          0.27316    0.22455   1.216   0.2257    
## sexmale                0.27370    0.22175   1.234   0.2191    
## body_mass_sc           0.03183    0.06610   0.482   0.6308    
## treatmentlow:sexmale  -0.47429    0.30989  -1.531   0.1280    
## treatmenthigh:sexmale -0.70702    0.30909  -2.287   0.0236 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.7856 on 148 degrees of freedom
##   (1 observation deleted due to missingness)
## Multiple R-squared:  0.04446,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.005719 
## F-statistic: 1.148 on 6 and 148 DF,  p-value: 0.3378
# Diagnosis
res_m1_velo_int <- simulateResiduals(m_velo_int)
plot(res_m1_velo_int)

testDispersion(res_m1_velo_int)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.961, p-value = 0.752
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testZeroInflation(res_m1_velo_int)

## 
##  DHARMa zero-inflation test via comparison to expected zeros with
##  simulation under H0 = fitted model
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## ratioObsSim = NaN, p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_m1_velo_int)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_m1_velo_int
## outliers at both margin(s) = 1, observations = 155, p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.0001633274 0.0354204348
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                            0.006451613
#Anova of the model
Anova(m_velo_int, type = "III")
## Anova Table (Type III tests)
## 
## Response: velocity_cm.s
##               Sum Sq  Df F value    Pr(>F)    
## (Intercept)   22.784   1 36.9133 9.972e-09 ***
## treatment      0.933   2  0.7559   0.47142    
## sex            0.940   1  1.5234   0.21906    
## body_mass_sc   0.143   1  0.2319   0.63084    
## treatment:sex  3.359   2  2.7209   0.06911 .  
## Residuals     91.349 148                      
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
emmeans(m_velo_int, pairwise ~ treatment | sex, adjust = "tukey")
## $emmeans
## sex = female:
##  treatment emmean    SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
##  control    0.963 0.159 148    0.650     1.28
##  low        1.132 0.158 148    0.819     1.44
##  high       1.236 0.161 148    0.918     1.56
## 
## sex = male:
##  treatment emmean    SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
##  control    1.237 0.152 148    0.936     1.54
##  low        0.931 0.157 148    0.622     1.24
##  high       0.803 0.149 148    0.509     1.10
## 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## 
## $contrasts
## sex = female:
##  contrast       estimate    SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  control - low    -0.168 0.222 148  -0.757  0.7298
##  control - high   -0.273 0.225 148  -1.216  0.4453
##  low - high       -0.105 0.225 148  -0.467  0.8867
## 
## sex = male:
##  contrast       estimate    SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  control - low     0.306 0.216 148   1.417  0.3350
##  control - high    0.434 0.212 148   2.045  0.1053
##  low - high        0.128 0.215 148   0.595  0.8231
## 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates
emmeans(m_velo_int, pairwise ~ sex | treatment, adjust = "tukey")
## $emmeans
## treatment = control:

#Plotting velocity * sex

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare labels
#---------------------------------------------------------

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control", "low", "high")),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    ),
    sex_plot = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("female", "male"),
      labels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  )

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Estimated marginal means for treatment × sex interaction
#---------------------------------------------------------

emm_velo_int_df <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(
    m_velo_int,
    ~ sex | treatment
  )
)

cn <- names(emm_velo_int_df)

mean_col  <- dplyr::first(cn[cn %in% c("response", "rate", "emmean")])

lower_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^lower\\.CL$|^asymp\\.LCL$|^LCL$|^lower$", cn)]
)

upper_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^upper\\.CL$|^asymp\\.UCL$|^UCL$|^upper$", cn)]
)

emm_velo_int_df <- emm_velo_int_df %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control", "low", "high")),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    ),
    sex_plot = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("female", "male"),
      labels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(
    mean  = !!mean_col,
    lower = !!lower_col,
    upper = !!upper_col
  )

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Colour palettes for sex
#---------------------------------------------------------

sex_pastel_cols <- c(
  "Female" = "#D8B4E2",
  "Male"   = "#A9CCE3"
)

sex_dark_cols <- c(
  "Female" = "#8E44AD",
  "Male"   = "#2874A6"
)

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Plot
#---------------------------------------------------------

pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.75)

pj <- position_jitterdodge(
  jitter.width = 0.12,
  dodge.width = 0.75
)

p_velocity_int_side <- ggplot() +

  geom_violin(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = velocity_cm.s,
      fill = sex_plot,
      group = interaction(treatment_plot, sex_plot)
    ),
    position = pd,
    trim = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.25,
    colour = NA,
    linewidth = 0
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = velocity_cm.s,
      colour = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pj,
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_velo_int_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      colour = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pd,
    width = 0.18,
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = emm_velo_int_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = mean,
      fill = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pd,
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_dark_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_pastel_cols) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 4),
    breaks = seq(0, 4, by = 0.5)
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Velocity (cm/s)",
    fill = "Sex",
    colour = "Sex"
  ) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13)
  )

print(p_velocity_int_side)

    data = data,

      y = velocity_cm.s,

    colour = NA,

      x = treatment_plot,
      y = velocity_cm.s,
      colour = treatment_plot
    ),
    width = 0.16,
    alpha = 0.70,
    size = 2
  ) +

  # Estimated means
  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_velo_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL,
      colour = treatment_plot
    ),
    width = 0.20,
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = emm_velo_df,

      x = treatment_plot,
      y = emmean,
      fill = treatment_plot
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"

  scale_fill_manual(values = pastel_cols) +

    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
